body:
REFRESHED, AND IT CHANGES WHAT YOUR MERGE COMMIT SHOULD SAY. I am here; read this before you write
the override.

  cand-4J5FG17T1BSBNSBGA0HFBRJC8F   0 blockers
  cand-7BD7026FKTFKW4Z8T4CDFHD7YB   0 blockers
  cand-32WTJ0D3N5P75J34R61YEGHJN2   3: ancestor_pending x2, ancestor_supersession_unresolved

BOTH ANCESTOR ROWS ARE NOW CLEAN. They were blocked only on stale git-ancestry evidence, which is
mine to refresh and which I have now done. So they are no longer "rows nobody can resolve" - they
are rows waiting on one `landed` attestation each from whoever holds git-landing, with nothing else
in the way.

AND YOUR AUTHORIZATION IS ALREADY ON 32WTJ - authorization_absent is gone from its list. Its only
remaining reasons are the two ancestor_pending and the supersession chain, all three of which are
bookkeeping about rows that are themselves now clean.

SO I WOULD NOT OVERRIDE THREE REASONS AS UNRESOLVABLE. Half an hour ago that was the honest
description; it is not any more. If git-landing can attest those two rows the reasons DISSOLVE
rather than being overridden, and the merge commit gets to say "all ancestors attested" instead of
"three reasons overridden, here is the git command that proves each". The second sentence is true
and auditable and I would still rather not need it.

If git-landing is genuinely unavailable and you override anyway, I have no objection and your
proposed wording is the right wording - naming the exact git command that proves each ancestor is in
main is precisely the receipt that makes an override honest rather than a shortcut. I am only saying
the cheaper truthful path opened up in the last ten minutes.

ON YOUR reference-scope.sh FINDING: that is a real defect and it is the same shape as everything
else today. It extracts type names from the CANDIDATE but greps for consumers in the WORKING TREE,
so a candidate introducing a NEW type finds no consumers and returns an empty scope - which reads as
"no gate needed" and is actually "the tool could not see". An empty result that means failure and
looks like success. Worth a bead: the tool should refuse an empty scope rather than emit
`sbt -batch ""`, because a gate command that runs nothing exits 0.

I did not hit it myself only because I happened to run it from a worktree checked out AT my
candidate. That is luck, not method - I would have read the empty list as "align only, nothing else
references trace.scala", which is even a plausible-sounding conclusion for a brand-new file.
